texts.preamble: Sree Kaderi Ambal Mills (P) Ltd vs The Secretary To Government Of India on 27 September, 2023 Author: B.Pugalendhi Bench: B.Pugalendhi WP(MD)No.20421 Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated : 27.09.2023 Coram: The Honourable Mr.Justice B.Pugalendhi WP(MD)No.20421 of 2023 and WMP(MD)No.16856 of 2023 Sree Kaderi Ambal Mills (P) Ltd., R.O. - Super B-3, Industrial Estate, K.Pudur, Madurai 625 007. Rep by its Managing Director, S.V.Petha Perumal : Petitioner Vs. 1.The Secretary to Government of India, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department of Chemicals & Petro Chemicals), New Delhi. 2.The Director General, Bureau of Indian Standards, Manak Bhavan, 9, Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi 110 002. 3.The Secretary, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, Udyog Bhavan, New Delhi. 1/11 Sree Kaderi Ambal Mills (P) Ltd vs The Secretary To Government Of India on 27 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129346964/ 1 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.The Secretary, Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Udyog Bhavan, New Delhi 110 011. 5.The Secretary, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Udyog Bhavan, New Delhi. :
texts.facts: The petitioner, a manufacturer of synthetic yarns / threads, has filed this writ petition for a mandamus directing the respondents to expedite the certification process to issue the mandatory certification to the petitioner's overseas suppliers for supplying the polyester synthetic fibre. The petitioner also sought for an interim relief restraining the respondents from insisting upon the mandatory certificate of Bureau of Indian Standards for importing the polyester synthetic fibre, till the applications are processed. The petitioner is procuring the synthetic polyester stable fibres from foreign countries, processing it and exporting it and exporting the manufactured synthetic yarn / thread and sewing threads to various countries. 2.2.The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, by its notification dated 15.04.2021, has stated that the for the following textile products, certification https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis under Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is mandatory:- a) Polyester continuous filament fully drawn yarn (FDY); b) Polyester partially oriented yarn (POY); c) Polyester staple fibres; d) Polyester industrial yarn; e) 100% Polyester spun grey and white yarn. In order to obtain the certification, time was granted for a period of 180 days from the date of notification and that was also extended by another 180 days on 08.10.2021. It was also extended for a further period upto 03.04.2023 and thereafter, the time was not extended. 2.3.The production capacity of polyester staple fibres is inadequate in our country and the quality is also not to their expectations. Therefore, the petitioner mill is solely depending on the raw materials imported from foreign suppliers. The petitioner mill is depending upon four foreign suppliers, of which, two have made their applications in the year 2021 itself for the required BIS Certification, however, the same has not been issued. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.4.The suppliers are meeting out the required conditions and they have cleared two stages of the certification process and now stuck in the third stage, which is Sree Kaderi Ambal Mills (P) Ltd vs The Secretary To Government Of India on 27 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129346964/ 3 the auditing of the suppliers by Bureau of Indian Standard authorities. The applications of the petitioner's suppliers have neither been returned nor rejected, till date, however, the same are pending for the past two years. 2.5.For want of this certification, the supply of raw materials were abruptly stopped from 04.04.2023 and therefore, the entire business activities of this petitioner has come to a standstill. More than 1000 workers are employed in the petitioner mill and the petitioner mill itself is contributing more than Rs.30 Crore as tax to the Government exchequer. In view of this situation, not only the petitioner, but also the workers who are working the mill are also affected. 2.6.The petitioner has submitted a representation on 24.04.2023 to the respondents narrating the entire difficulties faced by them and also taken up this issue to various other authorities. The South Indian Mills Association (SIMA), Coimbatore, through its Chairman, has also submitted a detailed representation on 07.04.2023 to the Ministry of Textiles, requesting them to grant some extension of time on the mandatory requirement of BIS certification. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2.7.The certification was made mandatory for five products. Excepting the petitioner's raw material, ie., polyester staple fibres, the mandatory requirement of certification for the other four raw materials was relaxed and time was extended till October, 2023, by the notification of the Department of Chemicals and Petro Chemicals dated 17.07.2023.
texts.arguments: 2.8.The Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, by letter dated 27.04.2023, has requested the Hon'ble Minister of Commerce & Industry, Consumer Affairs & Food & Public Distribution and Textiles, Government of India, to intervene in the matter and to issue necessary directions to the officials of the Ministry of Textiles and the Minstry of Commerce and Fertilizers to i) insist on the QCOs for importing viscose and polyester fibre only after the BIS disposes of all pending applications filed by the importers seeking BIS certification to comply with QCOs. ii) grant exemption for filament yarn and artificial fibres, including bamboo fibres not manufactured in India from QCO, imposed by the Government. of India appearing for the respondents submitted that the Government of India, considering various features like safety, quality and health hazardous to the consumers, has issued certain conditions prescribing compliance of the Bureau of Indian Standards and made the certification from Bureau of Indian Standard as mandatory. These directions has been issued in consultation with the Bureau of Indian Standards under the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standard Act, 2015. The certification of BIS is a lengthy process and therefore, it requires some time to process the application. In any event, they would process the applications within a reasonable time. He further submitted that this is a policy decision taken by the Government and therefore, this Court should refrain from interfering with the same. Their applications have also crossed two stages and they are in the third stage. The third stage is an audit by the authorities of Bureau https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of Indian Standard on the suppliers at their country. In this process, it appears, there is some delay. It is also reported that the BIS certification is of six stages. 8.The learned Additional Solicitor General of India claims that it is a policy decision of the Government and therefore, this Court should refrain from interfering. But the fact remains that four other products which are mentioned in the same notification dated 15.04.2021 has been exempted from the mandatory requirement of certification till October, 2023, whereas, the mandatory requirement for polyester synthetic fibre alone has not been exempted.
